source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: Astra/Sol models *do* seem to perform better on xhigh, for this benchmark
claim: The article adds a caveat the repo report lacks: Astra and Sol seem to do better at xhigh on this benchmark, so the medium-beats-xhigh result is model-specific (Opus 5.5 clearly), not universal.
evidence_detail: Single runs; Astra 29 to 32 strict at xhigh; but SOL 6 went 30 to 26 per the chart, so the article's Sol remark is looser than the data.
landing: Per-model effort routing, not a blanket downgrade of verifiers from xhigh to medium.
map_note: Caveat that Astra does better at xhigh, so medium-beats-xhigh is model-specific (Opus), not universal.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: XHigh costs 2.11-4.22x as much as Medium in the three complete pairs
claim: Xhigh cost 2.11x to 4.22x medium across the three complete model pairs, and Opus 5.5 did better at medium than at xhigh.
evidence_detail: Three pairs, one run each; Opus 28 vs 25 strict.
landing: Evidence for testing medium effort on harness verifiers and refuters.
map_note: Restates 2.11-4.22x xhigh cost across three pairs with Opus better at medium.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: I ran each model and effort setting once.
claim: Every model and effort setting was run exactly once (one campaign per setting, seed 42), so run-to-run variance is unmeasured and the effort comparisons are single samples.
evidence_detail: Repeated in the article, and the cost chart notes 'No repeated seeds'.
landing: A reminder to repeat harness-effort trials before acting on a single comparison, including P1.
map_note: Each setting run once, seed 42, so variance unmeasured and comparisons are single samples.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: One campaign per setting can't tell me how much is run-to-run variation.
claim: He explicitly says the effort result does not prove that more reasoning hurts coding, only that higher effort was not a reliable way to buy more strict passes.
evidence_detail: Hedge wording in the article, matching the report; the title still says 'considered harmful'.
landing: Treat the effort finding as hypothesis-grade when setting verifier effort.
map_note: Author hedges that the result does not prove more reasoning hurts; one campaign cannot separate variation.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: GPT-6.1 Medium has the lowest recorded cost at $178.51
claim: Cheapest campaign (GPT-6.1 SOL Medium, $178.51) matched Astra Medium's strict count, while Fable at about 8.68x the cost got three fewer strict passes, so cost and quality are decoupled.
evidence_detail: Recorded cost, not invoice; Fable $1,550.07 with 26 strict vs 29.
landing: Cost-per-verdict thinking when choosing models for reviewers.
map_note: Cheapest campaign ($178.51) matched Astra Medium strict count; Fable at ~8.68x cost got fewer strict passes.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: the benchmark should measure how much garbage models leave in the codebase.
claim: He reverses his first instinct to exclude scratch and temp files from quality scores after Gabe argued that if humans are not reading the code, leftover junk must be measured, so tests, scratch and generated copies get no free pass.
evidence_detail: Change of position, attributed to a chat with Gabe Orlanski.
landing: Closing checks should count leftover scratch files; a cleanliness gate on agent working directories.
map_note: Author reverses initial instinct to exclude scratch/temp files after Gabe's argument; same claim, position change recorded.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: If we're not reading the code, we need to measure it.
claim: If humans are not reading agent code, the output has to be measured by tooling, which is the case for backpressure and verifier scripts.
evidence_detail: Principle stated while defending the choice to include scratch code.
landing: Measured gates (lint, scanners) in place of self-reported compliance.
map_note: Principle: if not reading the code, measure it with tooling.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: Opus XHigh has the lowest slop percentage at 77.75%, versus 94.25% for Opus Medium.
claim: Opus 5.5 xhigh left the lowest slop coverage (77.75%) against 94.25% at medium, yet had fewer strict passes (25 vs 28), so effort trades test passing against code cleanliness.
evidence_detail: 28 matched problems, SLOC-weighted; single run per setting.
landing: Effort routing should depend on what the task needs (pass tests vs maintainability).
map_note: Opus XHigh 77.75% slop coverage vs 94.25% Medium with fewer strict passes; adds figures.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: Opus 5.5. XHigh wrote code that was close to ~5x cleaner.
claim: The article's pull-quote says xhigh code was about 5x cleaner despite fewer strict passes; this '~5x' framing is not backed by the 77.75 vs 94.25 percentage figures (about 3.6x lower unflagged share ratio at most), so the headline is loose.
evidence_detail: Pull-quote in both report and article; 5x is not derived from the stated percentages.
landing: Do not rely on the 5x figure; treat as directional.
map_note: The ~5x cleaner pull-quote is not backed by the 77.75 vs 94.25 percentages; headline is loose.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: These new models may produce new maintainability anti-patterns that we haven't built linters for yet
claim: The 200+ linter battery was built from patterns of earlier agent-authored PRs, so new models may produce slop that existing linters miss, which means a fixed verifier set goes stale.
evidence_detail: Speculation, with a promised follow-up from Gabe.
landing: Backpressure rules and verifier checklists need periodic refresh against new model output.
map_note: Fixed linter set goes stale as new models make anti-patterns not yet linted; one new linter per anti-pattern needed.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: We're getting better at maintaing a codebase over time (14.8% to 16.3% during may->september)
claim: Strict pass rate rose only 14.8% to 16.3% from May to September, and he expects 'keeping the lights on for a while to come', meaning slow gains in multi-checkpoint maintenance.
evidence_detail: Different subsets are not comparable; this uses the full benchmark v1.0 vs the May official figure.
landing: Plan for verifiers and human review to stay load-bearing; do not assume models drop the need.
map_note: 14.8% to 16.3% strict May to September; slow maintenance gains.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: the agents get the main behavior right much more often than they keep all tested behavior working
claim: Agents get core behavior right far more often than they keep all tested behavior working as requirements change (core 65.8-74.0% vs strict 12.2-16.3%), so regressions are the main failure mode.
evidence_detail: Ten complete campaigns, 196 checkpoints each.
landing: Regression-style verifiers over earlier work in each phase; cold-resume trial checks old facts survive.
map_note: Core 65.8-74.0% vs strict 12.2-16.3% across ten campaigns, 196 checkpoints; regressions dominate.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: 36 problems and 196 checkpoints per setting
claim: Sample size moved from 3 to 6 to 36 problems (196 checkpoints), so earlier subset results (including Fable's 30%) cannot be compared; he distrusts his own earlier small-subset numbers.
evidence_detail: Self-correction on comparability of earlier writeups.
landing: Do not generalise from small trials; state sample size next to every harness claim.
map_note: Sample moved 3 to 6 to 36 problems, so earlier subset results are not comparable; author distrusts his earlier numbers.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)

claim: For reproducibility he pins catalog version, prompt, seed, pass policy and Docker with Python 3.12 and uv, a pinned-conditions benchmark protocol.
evidence_detail: Repro recipe.
landing: Pin conditions when the harness runs its own effort or routing trials.
map_note: Pins catalog version, prompt, seed, pass policy and Docker with Python 3.12 and uv.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex

evidence_detail: Scoring rule.
landing: nowhere obvious
map_note: Each checkpoint builds on prior code and counts equally; early failures persist.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex

map_note: Top ranks are near-ties (Astra xhigh 32 vs 29); author's 'two checkpoints' wording is inconsistent with the table.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
author: Dex
quote: splitting code into more helper functions can lower average complexity without making the code easier to change
claim: Average complexity is gameable by splitting into helpers and fewer lines is not automatically better, so single metrics mislead and need to be read together.
evidence_detail: Caveat on the callables chart.

map_note: Average complexity gameable by splitting into helpers; single metrics mislead.

source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)

source_title: scb-3-effort.png
author: Dex

map_note: Chart footnote: medium and xhigh pairs differ in date and agent version, so effort is confounded; Opus Max and GPT-6.1 XHigh excluded.

source_title: scb-3-effort.png
author: Dex
quote: Medium to XHigh: Opus 28 to 25; Astra 29 to 32; GPT-6 SOL 30 to 26.

source_title: scb-3-pass-rates.png
author: Dex
quote: Strict scores stay low. Core success is much higher.
claim: Chart gives per-campaign strict/core counts out of 196 (e.g. Astra XHigh 32/136, SOL Medium 30/133, 6.1 SOL Medium 29/129, Opus Medium 28/145, Fable XHigh 26/142, GLM 24/130); the chart shows GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh core 139 while the report table lists 70.92% (consistent).
evidence_detail: Core counts from the chart, including 5.6 SOL XHigh 28/139 and Opus XHigh 25/141.
landing: nowhere obvious
map_note: Per-campaign strict/core counts out of 196; strict low, core much higher.

source_title: scb-3-pass-rates.png
author: Dex
quote: GLM labeled XHigh from saved config; directory says Max.
claim: The chart footnote admits GLM's effort label comes from saved config while its directory says Max, so one effort label is uncertain; Opus Max and GPT-6.1 XHigh were incomplete at capture.
evidence_detail: Chart footnote; not in the article or the report text.
landing: Verify which effort setting a run actually used.
map_note: GLM effort label uncertain (config says XHigh, directory says Max); Opus Max and GPT-6.1 XHigh incomplete; adds data-quality caveat.

source_title: scb-3-cost-strict.png
author: Dex
quote: Dates and agent versions differ.
claim: Cost scatter shows 10 campaigns spanning $178.51 to $1,550.07 inside a 12.24-16.33% strict band, with no repeated seeds; GLM 5.3 XHigh $365.13, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh $753.30; GPT-6.1 uses SOL pricing and Fable had two checkpoints with zero metering.
evidence_detail: Chart notes: recorded cost is not an invoice; Fable cost may be understated by the unmetered checkpoints.
landing: Cost estimates are approximate; do not over-fit routing on them.
map_note: Cost scatter: $178.51 to $1,550.07 inside a narrow strict band, no repeated seeds; Fable cost possibly understated.

source_title: scb-3-final-failures.png
author: Dex
quote: Final strict success does not imply every earlier checkpoint passed.
claim: Final failed test cases per campaign range from 1,435 (Astra XHigh) to 2,831 (SOL Medium), with final strict problems 0 to 3 of 36, so almost no run ends in a fully passing codebase; Skips: 5.6 XHigh 15, SOL6 XHigh 1, others 17.
evidence_detail: Failure categories: most final failures are Regression (e.g. 1,178 of 1,435; 2,479 of 2,831). Only last checkpoint per problem; not distinct bugs.
landing: Failures are mostly regressions of earlier behaviour; verifier should replay earlier tests.
map_note: Final failed tests 1,435 to 2,831 per campaign, mostly Regression; almost no run ends fully passing.

source_title: scb-3-final-failures.png
author: Dex
quote: Each problem contributes only its last expected checkpoint
claim: Opus 5.5 Medium, the core leader (145/196), ended with 0 of 36 strict final problems and 2,508 failed tests, so high core pass does not mean a working end state; Opus XHigh had 2,446 failed and 1 strict final.
evidence_detail: Chart numbers; GPT-6.1 SOL Medium 3/36 strict final with 2,757 failed.
landing: Judge the final state, not stage success.
map_note: Core leader Opus Medium ended 0/36 strict final problems with 2,508 failed tests; high core pass is not a working end state.

source_title: scb-3-quality-slop-coverage.png
author: Dex
quote: Ranked by SLOC-weighted heuristic coverage; not a defective-code percentage.
claim: Slop coverage per campaign (main=filtered except Opus Medium): Opus XHigh 77.75, Fable XHigh 82.11, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh 89.05, Astra XHigh 89.71, GLM 89.86, Astra Medium 90.76, SOL6 XHigh 91.11, 6.1 SOL Medium 91.51, SOL6 Medium 92.58, Opus Medium 94.25/92.90; no model is below 77%, and eight problems omitted for incomplete scanner coverage.
evidence_detail: Chart; 28 matched problems; coverage is a union of AST-rule spans and within-file clone spans over total SLOC.
landing: Quality scanners flag most lines for all models; a metric with little spread cannot gate.
map_note: Slop coverage 77.75 to 94.25 across campaigns, framed as heuristic coverage, not defect percentage.

source_title: scb-3-quality-volume.png
author: Dex
quote: Filtered is not a tests-free scope.
claim: Final source volume varies about 9x across campaigns: Opus Medium 216,881 SLOC (175,616 filtered + 41,265 in tests/_work), Fable XHigh 122,504, Opus XHigh 96,632, GLM 91,907, Astra XHigh 76,448, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh 66,186, 6.1 SOL Medium 44,019, SOL6 XHigh 41,147, Astra Medium 39,988, SOL6 Medium 24,991.
evidence_detail: Native Radon SLOC; no verified test/non-test split; only the Opus Medium snapshot (45 files in dynamic_buffer) changed under filtering.
landing: Output volume is a cheap bloat signal worth capping or monitoring.
map_note: Final source volume varies about 9x across campaigns; adds measured volume figures.

source_title: scb-3-quality-callables.png
author: Dex
quote: Callable count is not body length; complexity does not establish correctness.
claim: Callables and mean cyclomatic complexity differ widely: Fable 8,967 / 3.57, Astra XHigh 5,099 / 4.72, Opus XHigh 6,075 / 4.86, GLM 4,883 / 5.78, Astra Medium 2,438 / 6.38, 6.1 SOL Medium 2,531 / 6.38, Opus Medium 13,462 / 7.12, 5.6 SOL XHigh 2,331 / 7.47, SOL6 XHigh 1,803 / 8.74, SOL6 Medium 1,083 / 11.70.
evidence_detail: 28 matched problems; the chart calls the two measures separate, not a combined quality score.
landing: nowhere obvious
map_note: Models differ sharply in callable count and mean cyclomatic complexity; measures kept separate.

source_title: scb-3-quality-callables.png
author: Dex
quote: Missing scans never count as clean.
claim: Scanner policy: missing scans are never counted as clean and both scopes exclude dependency, venv and cache paths, a conservative rule for unmeasured output.
evidence_detail: Chart footnote across all three quality charts.
landing: Unknown-as-fail policy for verifiers, mirroring the 'unknown is not new' completion rule.
map_note: Scanner policy: missing scans never counted as clean, dependency/venv/cache paths excluded; no family covers conservative handling of unmeasured output.

landing: Briefing text for sub-agent/reviewer hand-backs in workflows
map_note: Harness wraps subagent hand-back as model output with no user authority; no family covers sub-agent-return injection defence.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: leverage and /show-me vs specs as long as code
author: Dex

evidence_detail: The 40:1 figure is the quoted third party's; Dex only endorses it.
landing: Review artefacts at higher abstraction (show-me style) in the PR/owner view
map_note: Endorses a 40:1 spec-to-code compression, against the claim that a spec as detailed as code is as long as the code.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: SCB pending results across new models

evidence_detail: Results are in images not visible here; no numbers in the text.

map_note: Re-benches SlopCodeBench on each new model; per-release re-measurement.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: performative tokenmaxxing

map_note: Performative token maximising criticised; token smarter not harder.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: SWE-sweep benchmark
author: Dex

source_title: @dexhorthy post: factories vs codebases
author: Dex
quote: everything you "ship out the door" impacts your ability to/ agility to ship the next thing

evidence_detail: Argument in reply to the factory-metaphor post; no data.
landing: Justifies per-PR refute-by-default review
map_note: Codebase past output affects future output, unlike a factory; cumulative quality gates.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: alpha in reviewing
author: Dex

map_note: Always alpha in reviewing, though the reviewed artifact may be plans rather than code; no review gives the same slop as everyone.

source_title: @dexhorthy post: context across sessions and handoff

source_title: @dexhorthy post: Anthropic in-house version control
author: Dex

source_title: Why Opus Medium Beats X-High at Writing Maintainable Code
author: Dex
quote: if you use medium, it's cheaper and better for Opus. But if you use medium for Astra, it's cheaper, but not as good.
claim: The effort effect is model-family specific: medium is cheaper and better for Opus, but for the OpenAI models (Astra) medium is cheaper and worse, so xhigh pays off there.

source_title: Why Opus Medium Beats X-High at Writing Maintainable Code
author: Dex

claim: Dex hedges his own effort finding live: the Claude-medium versus OpenAI-xhigh split may be an artefact of this benchmark, so it is not a general rule (the article says one campaign per setting cannot show variance).

source_title: Why Opus Medium Beats X-High at Writing Maintainable Code
